Fallback of 90 days' assistance offered in the comment.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
Section 11.3 gives us useful run-off rights (continued Customer access under Section 2, surviving support and maintenance, plus the Section 12 source code escrow), but the Agreement contains no post-termination transition-assistance right and no data return/export obligation. The only exit mechanic is a mutual "return or destroy" of Confidential Information at the disclosing party's option, with no format, no timescale and no deletion certification, which does not reach even the fallback (90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days). Because Commerce One hosts the MarketSite.net Service through which our Customers transact, our and our Customers' data can sit on its systems with no contractual route back to us. We therefore insert a new Section 11.4 at the preferred position: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days of request, and deletion with written certification thereafter, carved back for Commerce One's surviving obligations and legal retention so the new clause does not cut across the Section 11.3 run-off.

Original paragraphs:
p0098: 11.3 Effect of Termination. The following Sections shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason: 4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 14. Corio's right to allow its then-existing Customers and their Software Users to use and access the Software in accordance with Section 2 of this Agreement and all payment obligations related thereto shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement. Commerce One's obligation to provide Software support and maintenance to Corio and its Customers shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement, provided Corio continues to make its annual support and maintenance payments as specified in this Agreement. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.

Resolved definitions:
COMMERCE ONE: This License and Hosting Agreement (the "AGREEMENT") is made and entered into as of October 29, 1999 ("EFFECTIVE DATE") by and between Corio Inc., a Delaware corporation, having its principal place of business at 700 Bay Road, Suite 210, Redwood City, CA 94063 ("CORIO") and Commerce One, Inc., a Delaware corporation having its principal place of business at 1600 Rivera Avenue, Walnut Creek, CA 94596 ("COMMERCE ONE").
SOFTWARE USER: 1.1 "SOFTWARE USER" means a named user of the Corio Services worldwide to whom a user identification number and password has been assigned, which permits that user to access and use the Software on a designated Corio Server. The identification number and password used by a Software User is reusable and reassignable and may be used and transferred by Corio, in accordance with the licenses granted below, between Customers as one Customer discontinues the Corio Services and another Customer subscribes.
SOFTWARE: 1.10 "SOFTWARE" means Commerce One's proprietary software described in EXHIBIT A attached hereto and made a part hereof, in object code form only, and any Updates or Upgrades (as defined below) thereto.

Rendered redline:
p0098: 11.3 Effect of Termination. The following Sections shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason: 4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 14. Corio's right to allow its then-existing Customers and their Software Users to use and access the Software in accordance with Section 2 of this Agreement and all payment obligations related thereto shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement. Commerce One's obligation to provide Software support and maintenance to Corio and its Customers shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement, provided Corio continues to make its annual support and maintenance payments as specified in this Agreement. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
11.4 Transition Assistance and Return of Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, and in addition to its surviving obligations under Section 11.3, Commerce One shall: (a) at Corio's request, provide reasonable transition assistance to Corio and its Customers for a period of up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Corio's written request, return to Corio all data of Corio and its Customers then in Commerce One's possession or control, including all data generated through or stored in the MarketSite.net Service, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Corio in writing, except to the extent retention is required to perform Commerce One's surviving obligations under this Agreement or by applicable law.

Comment:
[Playbook] We have added a short exit provision requiring transition assistance for up to six months at Commerce One's then-current rates and return of our and our Customers' data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, with deletion and certification thereafter. Our playbook requires a data-return and transition right on exit; we can work with 90 days of assistance if six months is an issue.

[{"id":"f-indemn-cc763401","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8 INDEMNIFICATION.","rationale":"Section 8 contains a one-way vendor indemnity in our favour: Commerce One must indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers against third-party claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights, with a standard procedure (prompt notice, tender of control to the vendor at its expense and counsel, cooperation at vendor's cost, plus a right for us to join with our own counsel). Exclusions are narrow and conventional (use other than as set out in the Documentation; modification by a party other than Commerce One where the infringement would not otherwise have occurred), and the remedy ladder is the usual procure / replace or modify / terminate and refund a pro-rated portion of fees paid. Section 9 expressly carves Section 8 out of both the 12-month fees cap and the consequential-damages exclusion, so the indemnity is uncapped — better for us than the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap. There is no Corio-side indemnity anywhere in the agreement, so the \"narrow Customer indemnity\" limb is satisfied by omission. The clause therefore meets the fallback (indeed exceeds it on the cap) and is compliant; no redline. Noted for the record only as sub-element gaps short of the preferred position: the indemnity does not extend to vendor breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to or disclosure of our data caused by the vendor, or vendor gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and the refund is tied to fees \"paid\" rather than \"paid or payable\". Given the uncapped IP indemnity and the absence of any reciprocal indemnity from us, these are not worth negotiating capital.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-6bc7355a","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13 SHARED RESOURCES.","rationale":"Section 13.5 starts in the right place — Developments created solely by Corio are owned by Corio and Commerce One assigns any claim it would otherwise have (p0116) — and Section 2.8 correctly limits Commerce One to its own Software, which is acceptable. The failure is the carve-out: where Commerce One supports a Development on an ongoing basis, Commerce One \"will retain all ownership rights, including intellectual property rights in the Developments\", with no licence back to Corio. That is an effective transfer of our own hosting-integration IP to the vendor and sits in walk-away territory, and it fails the fallback because Corio is left with no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free right to use or modify code it created and paid for. The redline deletes only the carve-out, leaving Commerce One's pre-existing materials and the Software untouched. Two lesser points noted but not separately flagged: the agreement has no express Customer Data / hosted customer data ownership statement, and the final sentence of 13.5 leaves ownership of enhancements to the Software itself to future negotiation — both can be raised as drafting points if the counterparty reopens Section 13.","proposal":"Delete the carve-out in Section 13.5 that transfers ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-90da358d","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY.","rationale":"Section 9 is facially mutual and excludes indirect/consequential damages, but it fails the fallback on two material terms. First, the cap base is not 12 months' fees: it is limited to amounts \"ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO ... FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO\", which reduces the cap to a per-transaction slice of fees and can fall well below six months' fees. Second, the only carve-out is \"LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8\" (Commerce One's IP indemnity, which in any event runs only in our favour); there is no carve-out for breach of the confidentiality obligation in Section 10 / the concurrent NDA, gross negligence or wilful misconduct, all of which the fallback requires. Our redline keeps the mutual structure, sets the cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000, adds an Excluded Claims definition covering indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirms Corio's fee obligations are not capped damages. Note also the duplicated/garbled text at p0092 should be deleted as a scrivener's error in engrossing.","proposal":"Make the mutual cap the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000, and add Excluded Claims carve-outs (indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement).","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-299f4c5c","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"SALES AND MARKETING COOPERATION","rationale":"No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Corio anywhere in the Agreement, so the clause set meets the preferred position. The Grant of Rights licenses are all expressly \"nonexclusive\" and impose only scope/IP restrictions (Section 2.7) rather than any requirement that Corio host, promote or source only Commerce One procurement software; Section 2.9 (New Products) merely contemplates future licences on terms to be agreed. The Exhibit D sales and marketing cooperation efforts (Relationship Managers, joint marketing, marketing fund, dedicated personnel) are stated to be \"non-binding\", and the only commitment there — commercially reasonable efforts to obtain two initial Customers (para 7) — is a soft effort obligation, not exclusive dealing. Section 13 (Shared Resources) is likewise non-restrictive and Section 13.6 expressly preserves each party's independent development rights. The only exclusivity-flavoured terms run in our favour (Section 2.4: Commerce One shall not contact Corio Customers regarding non-ASP licence sales and must refer them to Corio), which is acceptable and not flagged. Corio therefore retains full freedom to procure and host competing applications; no redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-8550a0de","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 11 TERM AND TERMINATION.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee on Corio, the licensee/customer, so it meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties). Section 11.2 permits termination for uncured material breach or insolvency with no minimum fee, fee acceleration or termination charge, and Section 11.3's surviving payment obligations attach only to Corio's continued use of the Software for existing Customers. Section 4 and Exhibit B/Section 17 Payment Terms contain only actual license, maintenance, MarketSite access, percentage revenue-share and capped time-and-materials fees, with no late-payment interest or penalty rate. Exhibit B revenue sharing is a percentage of actual revenue with limitations favouring Corio and no minimum volume commitment or make-whole payment. Two mechanics were considered and are not liquidated damages: (i) Section 4.4's audit \"shortfall\" payment is a true-up of amounts genuinely owed, and the >5% underpayment trigger shifts only the reasonable actual cost of the examination, which is cost reimbursement rather than a stipulated sum; and (ii) Exhibit C's response and resolution commitments run against Commerce One, with no penalties flowing from Corio. Nothing approaches the walk-away territory of damages exceeding remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches. No redline is required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-f856c7b0","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS.","rationale":"The Section 2 grants are strong on revocability and term: the hosting licence (2.1) is \"perpetual and irrevocable\" and the internal use licence (2.2) is \"royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual\", with no vendor right to revoke at will, and Section 14.1 permits assignment (and so transfer to a successor) in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets — meeting the fallback's transfer element. However, the grants run to Corio only: the word \"Affiliate\" appears nowhere in the Agreement, and 2.2 is limited to \"Corio's internal business operations\", so our affiliates have no coverage and no notice-based path to be added. That fails the fallback (\"affiliates covered on written notice\") on a material term. Contractor use is only indirectly supported (Section 14.8 subcontracting and the definition of Corio Servers as servers \"owned or operated by or for Corio\"), so we have made that express in the same edit. We therefore added an Affiliate definition and extended the 2.1 and 2.2 grants to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf; the remaining licences (2.3-2.5) flow from these grants and need no further change.","proposal":"Extend the Section 2 licences to Corio's Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf, and add an Affiliate definition","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-5ee0c171","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS.","rationale":"The agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use covenant binding Corio (our party). Section 2.7 (\"Restrictions\", p0042) limits only copying, reproduction and reverse engineering of the licensed Software — ordinary IP protection, not a restraint on our business. The \"CORIO MARKET SEGMENT\" (p0013) and \"TERRITORY\" (p0024) definitions merely delimit the scope of the licenses granted to us (and Section 2.10 lets us seek worldwide expansion), rather than prohibiting us from operating any business or buying/building competing products. Section 13.6 (p0117) affirmatively preserves each party's right to develop independently, and Exhibit D's sales and marketing cooperation is expressly non-binding. The only \"competitor\" reference (Section 14.1 assignment consent) is mutual and does not restrict our operations. Absence of any customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback (60–90 days' notice with a capped fee). We therefore added a new 11.2 giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no termination penalty, matching the preferred position; the fallback of 60 days' notice is available if needed. Noted but not separately flagged: Commerce One's non-renewal notice is 30 days rather than the preferred 90 days, but that is an end-of-term non-renewal right (mutual), not a mid-term convenience exit, so we have not redlined it here.","proposal":"Add Corio right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-646c5e2b","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 4 FEES.","rationale":"Section 4.4 is the only provision giving Commerce One inspection rights over our (Corio's) books, and it already meets the preferred position on every material term: frequency is capped at once each calendar year; inspections must be at reasonable times (i.e. no unannounced visits) and on reasonable notice; they are conducted by an independent certified public accountant who must be reasonably acceptable to us; Commerce One bears all costs unless an underpayment exceeds 5%; and the right is limited to books and records with no access to our systems or premises-level data. The only sub-element short of the preferred wording is that notice is expressed as \"reasonable notice\" rather than a fixed 30 days (fallback 15 days), and the auditor is not expressly bound by a confidentiality undertaking beyond its professional duties. Both are minor mechanics that do not defeat the fallback, so we are not redlining; we would accept a quantified notice period if the clause is reopened for other reasons.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-016810da","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14 MISCELLANEOUS.","rationale":"Section 14.3 selects California law, an accepted jurisdiction under the fallback position (Delaware or California law and courts), and places the forum in San Francisco County, California, with judgments enforceable in the San Francisco courts. The mandatory AAA arbitration is seated domestically in California, so it does not raise the walk-away concern of a foreign seat or exclusive foreign venue, and the jurisdiction is not the counterparty's foreign home forum. The clause therefore sits at the fallback rather than the preferred position (New York law and the state and federal courts in New York County); the substitution of binding domestic arbitration for a pure court forum is a sub-element short of preferred wording and is noted here rather than redlined, particularly as the California seat is convenient to us.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-f41e380c","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 4 FEES.","rationale":"No most-favoured-nation or price/terms-matching obligation exists anywhere in the Agreement. Fees (Section 4, Exhibit B pricing, revenue sharing and payment terms) are fixed figures negotiated between the parties, with no requirement that Corio (our party, as licensee/customer) extend to Commerce One any better pricing, revenue share or other terms granted to third parties, and no obligation to match third-party offers. Searches for \"most favored/favourable\", \"no less favorable\", \"lowest\", \"best price\", \"comparable\", \"similarly situated\", \"discount\" and \"any other customer\" returned nothing, and the grant, marketing (Exhibit D) and shared-resources provisions contain no MFN mechanic. This sits at the playbook's preferred position (no MFN burdening the Customer), so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-e97ac94f","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"PRICING","rationale":"This meets the preferred position: the agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, or volume commitment on Corio. Our payment obligations are limited to (i) the one-time BuySite license fee due on Software Acceptance, (ii) annual maintenance/support and MarketSite.net access fees for services actually made available, and (iii) a revenue share calculated on actual Application Management Revenue received from Corio Customers — i.e., pure pass-through of realized usage, with no floor, no guaranteed minimum, and no shortfall penalty. Exhibit B expressly sets Software Users at \"Unlimited,\" so there is no volume cap on our usage either.\n\nThree points noted but not flagged. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Corio / Commerce One)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Corio) 
**Re:** Contract review findings and proposed redlines

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. On balance the risk allocation is workable: the vendor IP indemnity in Section 8 is one-way in our favour and uncapped (Section 9 carves it out of both the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion), and the Agreement imposes no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-volume commitment or liquidated damages on us. Auto-renewal (12-month renewals, 30-day mutual notice) and the California law/San Francisco AAA forum are acceptable, the latter at the fallback.

Six items require action. Three are critical or high and, on our reading, sit in walk-away territory or fail the fallback on material terms: (i) the Section 13.5 carve-out that transfers ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back; (ii) the absence of any mid-term termination-for-convenience right across a five-year committed term; and (iii) the absence of any vendor insurance covenant. In addition, the Section 9 cap is measured by amounts actually paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to" rather than 12 months' fees, and carves out only Section 8 — with nothing for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The Section 2 licences run to Corio alone ("Affiliate" appears nowhere), and the Section 7.3 warranty runs only 60 days from the Effective Date with a 31 December 1999 sunset, so it can expire on or before acceptance. The Agreement also has no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation, which matters because Commerce One hosts the MarketSite.net Service. Assignment consent (Section 14.1) needs only a reasonableness standard and an affiliate carve-out.

One item — non-solicitation — could not be verified and is carried as needs review pending sight of the separately executed NDA and Statement of Work referenced in Section 14.10.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 8 INDEMNIFICATION. | One-way vendor IP indemnity in our favour with standard defence procedure; uncapped via the Section 9 carve-out, so better than the fallback super-cap. No redline. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 SHARED RESOURCES. | Section 13.5 correctly vests Corio-created Developments in Corio, but the carve-out gives Commerce One all ownership where it supports a Development on an ongoing basis, with no licence back. Walk-away territory; fails the fallback. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. | Cap is limited to amounts actually paid for the related transaction rather than 12 months' fees, and the sole carve-out is Section 8 (which runs only in our favour); no carve-out for confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. | Grants are perpetual and irrevocable and survive an M&A transfer under Section 14.1, but run to Corio only — "Affiliate" appears nowhere and 2.2 is limited to Corio's internal business operations. Fails the fallback affiliate limb. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | Five-year initial term with automatic one-year renewals; exits are limited to non-renewal and breach/insolvency. No customer convenience right — walk-away territory. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | SALES AND MARKETING COOPERATION | No sole-supplier or exclusive-dealing obligation on Corio; licences are non-exclusive and Exhibit D cooperation is expressly non-binding. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS. | Section 2.7 restricts only copying and reverse engineering; Section 13.6 preserves independent development. Preferred position. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | No penalty, early-termination fee or minimum payment on us; the Section 4.4 shortfall is a true-up and the >5% trigger shifts only actual examination cost. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER. | Conformance and no-malicious-code warranties with a real remedy ladder, but only 60 days from the Effective Date with a 31 December 1999 sunset — below the 90-day fallback and capable of expiring on or before acceptance. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | Section 11.3 run-off and Section 12 escrow are useful, but there is no transition-assistance right and no data return/export obligation beyond return-or-destroy of Confidential Information. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review | § 10 CONFIDENTIALITY. | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant binds Corio in this document. Verification did not pass: the separately executed NDA and Statement of Work incorporated by Section 14.10 are not before us. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 4 FEES. | Section 4.4 meets the preferred position (annual cap, reasonable time and notice, independent CPA reasonably acceptable to us, vendor cost absent >5% underpayment, books and records only). |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | California law, San Francisco County forum, domestic AAA seat — at the fallback, not the counterparty's home foreign forum. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 4 FEES. | No MFN, price-matching or no-less-favourable obligation anywhere; fees are fixed negotiated figures. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | PRICING | No minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall penalty; revenue share is on actual revenue and Exhibit B sets Software Users at "Unlimited". |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 11 TERM AND TERMINATION. | Twelve-month renewals with a mutual 30-day notice window (preferred position); Exhibit B fixes fees for Year 2–5 and beyond. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | Mutual, with an M&A carve-out and no change-of-control trigger, but consent is at absolute discretion with no reasonableness standard and no affiliate carve-out. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 MISCELLANEOUS. | No insurance clause; the only use of "insurance" is in the revenue definition. Commerce One hosts the Service and handles Corio and Customer data. Walk-away territory. |

## Walk-away items

The following are identified in our findings as walk-away territory and should be resolved before signature:

1. **Section 13.5 ownership carve-out (IP).** Transferring ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One wherever it provides ongoing support, with no licence back, is an effective transfer of our own hosting-integration IP. Our redline deletes only the carve-out, leaving Commerce One's pre-existing materials and the Software untouched.
2. **No termination for convenience (T4C).** A five-year committed term with no mid-term customer exit. We propose a new Section 11.2 giving Corio a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no penalty; 60 days' notice is available as a fallback.
3. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE).** We propose a new Section 14.10 (Insurance): CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request; fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M offered in the comment.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redlines** on the six action items: Section 13.5 (delete the ownership carve-out); Section 9 (mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, plus Excluded Claims for indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmation that fee obligations are not capped damages); Section 2 (extend the 2.1 and 2.2 licences to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, with an Affiliate definition); Section 11 (convenience termination and new Section 11.4 transition assistance up to six months at then-current rates, data return within 30 days in machine-readable format, deletion with written certification, carved back for surviving and legal-retention obligations); Section 7.3 (warranty of 12 months from acceptance, fallback 90 days from acceptance); Section 14.1 (reasonableness standard plus affiliate carve-out); and the new insurance covenant.
2. **Close the non-solicit diligence point.** Obtain the NDA and Statement of Work incorporated by Section 14.10 and confirm neither contains a non-solicit. If one is later proposed, our fallback is a mutual 12-month restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.
3. **Flag the engrossing point.** Ask counterparty to delete the duplicated/garbled text at p0092 in Section 9 as a scrivener's error.
4. **Hold in reserve, to raise only if the relevant clause reopens:** an express Customer Data / hosted customer data ownership statement and the unresolved ownership of Software enhancements in the final sentence of Section 13.5; a quantified audit notice period in Section 4.4; and a renewal reminder and price-uplift cap in Section 11.1. We are not spending negotiating capital on these, nor on the indemnity sub-elements (law, data, gross negligence, "paid or payable"), given the uncapped IP indemnity and absence of any reciprocal indemnity from us."}
